dish: Stone-milled cheung fun (rice rolls) coloured with spinach & dragonfruit
address: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-22, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
w: A father-and-son team from Shenzhen mill their own rice flour on a stone grinder to make thicker, rustic cheung fun to order, tinted naturally with spinach and pink dragonfruit across 13 fillings — a standout of the reopened (Aug 2025) Toa Payoh West hawker centre.

dish: Fried fish ban mian ($3) in savoury soup with handmade noodles
address: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, #02-24, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
w: A no-frills stall doing a $3 bowl of fried fish ban mian — crispy fried fish slices, handmade noodles and a clean savoury broth — one of the value picks flagged across guides to the renovated Toa Payoh West food centre.

dish: Handmade mee hoon kueh & sliced fish soup (20-year stall)
address: Toa Payoh West Market & Food Centre, Blk 127 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, S310127
w: A 20-year veteran hand-tearing mee hoon kueh dough to order and ladling fish soup and porridge — old-school comfort noodles that regulars queue for at Toa Payoh West.

dish: $6 dum-cooked chicken/mutton/fish briyani with sambal
address: Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, #01-79, Blk 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210
w: The Toa Payoh outlet of the Tekka Centre briyani institution — a Michelin Plate / Michelin-recommended name whose fragrant $6 chicken, mutton and fish briyani draw a queue; the pull-apart rice and house sambal are the draw.

dish: $5 herbal-braised kway chap with pig offal & silky rice sheets
address: Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, #01-24, Blk 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210
w: A 40-year Toa Payoh institution famous for selling out fast — owner Mr Ng meticulously cleans the offal for an odourless, tender braise served over silky rice sheets in a light herbal broth; widely rated among Singapore's best kway chap.

dish: Aburi salmon maki & butter-yaki seabass bento (under $10) by an ex-hotel chef
address: 211 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, #01-01, S310211
w: An ex-hotel chef plates restaurant-grade Japanese food from a kopitiam beside the Lorong 8 hawker centre — the Tataki Salmon Roll ($6) and Butter Yaki Seabass Bento ($6.80) look far pricier than they cost; nothing on the menu tops $10.

dish: Penang-style white & cockle fried kway teow with heavy wok hei
n: Da Lao Fried White Kway Teow
address: Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, #01-23, Blk 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210
w: A one-man wok turning out Penang-style fried white kway teow with serious wok hei — clean, coated-not-greasy strands with fish cake, lap cheong and cockles from $4; the single-hand pace means a wait, and a long queue.

dish: Hand-torn sheng mian / mee hoon kway in pork & ikan bilis broth
n: Seletar Sheng Mian Mee Hoon Kway
address: Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, Blk 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210
w: Relocated from the demolished Seletar market, this snaking-queue stall hand-kneads, smacks and tears each piece of dough for uniquely textured sheng mian in a comforting pork-and-ikan-bilis broth from $3.

dish: Cendol with tightly-packed shaved ice, pandan jelly, gula melaka & Mao Shan Wang durian
address: Toa Payoh Lorong 8 Market & Food Centre, #01-07, Blk 210 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, S310210
w: Widely dubbed the best cendol in Singapore — and a favourite of ESM Goh Chok Tong, whose photos line the stall — with firmly-packed ice that stays solid, springy pandan jelly and gula melaka, plus Mao Shan Wang / D24 durian tops.

dish: Teochew mee pok with handmade yellowtail fishballs & fish dumplings
n: Song Kee Kway Teow Noodle Soup
address: Toa Payoh Lorong 5 Food Centre, Blk 75 Lorong 5 Toa Payoh, S310075
w: A 16-year evening-only stall (5pm–midnight) whose fishballs are pounded from scratch at 3am — bouncy, fresh yellowtail fishballs and fragrant fish dumplings over springy mee pok that fans call the best in Singapore.

dish: 3rd-generation charcoal-grilled chicken & pork satay (since 1966)
address: Toa Payoh Lorong 5 Food Centre, #01-25, Blk 75 Lorong 5 Toa Payoh, S310075
w: A 1966 satay stall now in its third generation, grilling well-marinated Chinese-style chicken and pork skewers over charcoal to order — beautifully charred sticks served with peanut sauce and fresh pineapple gravy.

dish: Orh chien (fried oyster omelette) with large Korean oysters
address: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, #01-25, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022
w: A 50-year-old orh chien specialist (open ~3 hours a day) frying crisp-yet-chewy potato-starch batter with fluffy egg and juicy large Korean oysters, finished with crunchy parsley — a repeat pick on 'best oyster omelette' lists.

dish: Fried bee hoon breakfast plate with runny sunny-side-up egg
address: Kim Keat Palm Market & Food Centre, Blk 22 Lorong 7 Toa Payoh, S310022
w: The stall with Kim Keat Palm's longest breakfast queue — wok-fried bee hoon and noodles with cabbage, best paired with a runny-yolk sunny-side-up egg; a heartland morning staple.

dish: Braised pork-innards kway chap (2nd-gen, since 1967)
address: Toa Payoh Palm Spring Market, Blk 93 Lorong 4 Toa Payoh, S310093
w: A second-generation kway chap running since 1967 and rated Singapore's best-rated kway chap — spice-forward braised innards, tau pok and silky rice sheets from 5.30pm, with snaking queues before it even opens.

dish: 58-year Teochew mee pok with handmade fishballs & meatballs
address: Toa Payoh Palm Spring Market, Blk 93 Lorong 4 Toa Payoh, S310093
w: A 58-year cult favourite with arguably the longest queue in Palm Spring from 6am — springy mee pok tossed in a punchy chilli sauce with hand-made fishballs and meatballs; dry or soup.

dish: Cheese prata & mee goreng (Makansutra 'Divine' rating)
address: Toa Payoh Vista Market, 74 Lorong 4 Toa Payoh, S310074
w: A Vista Market morning fixture drawing daily queues for crisp roti prata — plain to cheese-and-egg and sweet banana — then Indian-Muslim mee goreng, nasi goreng merah and tulang merah after 1.30pm; carries a Makansutra 'Divine' rating.

dish: You-tiao-heavy Chinese rojak with prawn paste, torch ginger & cuttlefish
address: Gourmet Paradise Food Court, Toa Payoh HDB Hub, #B1-01, Blk 480 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, S310480
w: A decades-old rojak stall by the HDB Hub food-court escalator with a permanent 20-30 minute queue — a generous mountain of youtiao, cucumber, pineapple, turnip and cuttlefish drowned in prawn-paste, torch-ginger and mounds of peanut.

dish: Hand-slapped biang biang noodles & rou jia mo
n: Biang Biang Noodles Xi'an Famous Food
address: Food Alley, 190 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, #01-518, Toa Payoh Central, S310190
w: A rare hawker source of Xi'an biang biang noodles — extra-wide belt noodles hand-stretched and slapped against the counter, tossed with braised pork, tomato-egg and chilli, plus rou jia mo (Chinese 'burger'); a hidden gem at Toa Payoh Central's Food Alley.

dish: Wok-hei zi char (sambal kang kong, prawn-paste chicken, cereal pork)
address: Blk 73 Lorong 4 Toa Payoh, #01-585, S310073
w: A young-hawker zi char revival — five friends in their late twenties reopened a founder's father's stall, cooking almost a hundred dishes rich in wok hei at hawker prices, from sambal kang kong to inventive Imperial Cereal Milk Pork.

dish: 8-hour beef pho & fried pork-and-prawn spring rolls
address: Blk 125 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, #01-, S310125
w: A husband-and-wife stall (she's Vietnamese) doing soul-comforting pho with broth simmered 8 hours on beef shank and shin, plus crisp fried spring rolls stuffed with pork, prawn and glass noodles — sauces imported from Vietnam, everything under $10.

dish: Earl grey lavender / sea-salt gula melaka ice cream with thick Belgian waffles
address: Blk 128 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, #01-829, S310128
w: The original heartland home of a beloved SG ice-cream name — handcrafted scoops like Earl Grey Lavender and Sea Salt Gula Melaka over freshly-pressed, crisp-outside pillowy Belgian waffles; the Toa Payoh dessert stop.

dish: Handmade tiger-bread bakes, all-day breakfast & Nyonya chendol waffle
address: Blk 128 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, #01-833, S310128
w: An under-rated heartland cafe run by a France-trained baker — everything is handmade in-house, from crusty tiger bread and light not-too-sweet cakes to a Nyonya chendol waffle; a quaint wooden-front hideout beside Creamier.

dish: Watermelon rose cake & fudgy brownies
address: Blk 85C Lorong 4 Toa Payoh, #01-385, S310085
w: A hole-in-the-wall HDB cake cafe by three pastry-chef friends selling atas bakes from $3.50 — the chio Watermelon Rose cake (a nod to Black Star Pastry) and fudgy brownies among biscotti, pound cakes and cookies.
